cues.en: This episode is sponsored by Audible.
cues.zh: 本期节目由 Audible 赞助。

cues.en: Can reality be adjusted
cues.zh: 现实可以被调整吗

cues.en: after events have occurred?
cues.zh: 在事件发生之后？

cues.en: That's the unsettling implication of the delayed choice
cues.zh: 这就是延迟选择

cues.en: quantum eraser experiment.
cues.zh: 量子擦除实验令人不安的含义。

cues.en: We recently talked about the weird results of the single particle double slit experiment.
cues.zh: 我们最近谈过单粒子双缝实验的怪异结果。

cues.en: They imply some startling things about the nature of reality.
cues.zh: 它们暗示了现实本质的一些惊人之处。

cues.en: Today,
cues.zh: 今天，

cues.en: I wanna talk about an additional,
cues.zh: 我想谈谈另一个

cues.en: possibly even stranger version of this experiment
cues.zh: 这个实验甚至可能更奇怪的版本

cues.en: whose results force us to reconsider
cues.zh: 它的结果迫使我们重新思考

cues.en: the nature of causality itself.
cues.zh: 因果性本身的本质。

cues.en: Now, this episode isn't gonna make a lot of sense unless you've seen the first one, so go ahead and watch it if you haven't already. I'll wait right here.
cues.zh: 这一集如果你没看过第一集，可能不太好懂，所以还没看的话先去看看吧。我就在这儿等你。

cues.en: Okay? So the single particle double slit experiment suggests that things may not exist as well defined, even real particles
cues.zh: 好吧？那么单粒子双缝实验表明，事物也许并不以明确定义的形式存在，甚至算不上真正的粒子

cues.en: in that strange interim between creation and detection.
cues.zh: 在它产生与被探测之间那段奇特的过渡期里。

cues.en: There's a fuzzy space in which we don't know the particle's location or path.
cues.zh: 存在一个模糊的空间，我们不知道粒子在那里位于何处、走了哪条路径。

cues.en: The Copenhagen interpretation
cues.zh: 哥本哈根诠释

cues.en: would tell us that in this space,
cues.zh: 会告诉我们，在这个空间里，

cues.en: a particle is only its wave function,
cues.zh: 粒子仅仅是它的波函数，

cues.en: a distribution of possible properties.
cues.zh: 也就是可能属性的分布。

cues.en: It's a probability wave
cues.zh: 它是一种概率波

cues.en: that does all the usual wave like stuff,
cues.zh: 会表现出波通常会有的一切行为，

cues.en: like making interference patterns,
cues.zh: 比如形成干涉图样，

cues.en: until something happens to collapse it. At that point, the Copenhagen interpretation tells us that a true transition happens between wave and particle.
cues.zh: 直到某件事发生使它坍缩。这时，哥本哈根诠释告诉我们，波与粒子之间发生了真正的转变。

cues.en: But is that right?
cues.zh: 但这是对的吗？

cues.en: And if so, what really causes this transition?
cues.zh: 如果确实如此，那究竟是什么真正导致了这种转变？

cues.en: Does observation of the particle's location
cues.zh: 对粒子位置的观测

cues.en: force
cues.zh: 会迫使

cues.en: universe into settling down
cues.zh: 宇宙安定下来

cues.en: and deciding which particular reality we happen to be in?
cues.zh: 并决定我们恰好身处哪一个特定现实吗？

cues.en: To head off any wild metaphysical giddiness, I wanna say right now that there's absolutely no reason to believe that observation by a physicist
cues.zh: 为避免任何天马行空的形而上学眩晕，我现在先说明：完全没有理由相信，物理学家的观测

cues.en: is better at collapsing wave functions than observation by an electronic detector
cues.zh: 在使波函数坍缩方面，会比电子探测器的观测更有效

cues.en: or a house plan for that matter.
cues.zh: 甚至比一株室内植物更有效。

cues.en: We'll talk about what observation really means at a later point.
cues.zh: 我们稍后再讨论“观测”到底意味着什么。

cues.en: But it's still pretty interesting to see what happens if we try to observe the wave function at different points in the double slit experiment.
cues.zh: 但看看在双缝实验中，如果我们尝试在不同位置观测波函数会发生什么，仍然很有意思。

cues.en: The great mystery of the experiment
cues.zh: 这个实验最大的谜团

cues.en: is that very particle like things
cues.zh: 在于那些非常像粒子的东西

cues.en: appear to traverse both slits simultaneously,
cues.zh: 似乎同时穿过了两条缝，

cues.en: like you might expect of a wave.
cues.zh: 就像你会预期波所做的那样。

cues.en: Physicists love a good mystery and so have tried very, very hard to peek to see which slit these particles actually travel through
cues.zh: 物理学家喜欢有趣的谜团，所以非常非常努力地想去偷看这些粒子到底穿过哪条缝，

cues.en: before they produce the famous interference pattern. Turns out the universe is onto us.
cues.zh: 在它们产生著名的干涉图样之前。结果发现，宇宙早就看穿我们了。

cues.en: Any experiment that determines unambiguously
cues.zh: 任何能够明确判定

cues.en: which slit the particle traverses
cues.zh: 粒子经过哪条狭缝的实验

cues.en: destroys the interference pattern.
cues.zh: 都会破坏干涉图样。

cues.en: Instead,
cues.zh: 相反，

cues.en: particles land in simple clumps,
cues.zh: 粒子只会落成简单的团块，

cues.en: one for each slit,
cues.zh: 每条狭缝对应一团，

cues.en: as though they were traveling as simple particles the whole time.
cues.zh: 就好像它们自始至终都是普通粒子一样。

cues.en: This is even true if you place detectors on the far side of the slits
cues.zh: 即便你把探测器放在狭缝的远侧，也同样如此

cues.en: after the wave particle thing should have already been interfering with itself.
cues.zh: 而这时波粒二象性那套按理说早该开始自我干涉了。

cues.en: Just like the wave function is collapsing
cues.zh: 就好像波函数正在坍缩

cues.en: retroactively,
cues.zh: 而且是回溯性地，

cues.en: as if the universe is saying,
cues.zh: 仿佛宇宙在说：

cues.en: okay, guys, the human figured out which way you went. No more funny stuff. Better pretend like you were particles that whole time. But there's a huge problem with this interpretation.
cues.zh: 好吧，伙计们，人类已经弄清楚你们走的是哪条缝了。别再搞花样了。最好假装你们一直都是粒子。但这种解释有个巨大的问题。

cues.en: It's impossible to make these measurements
cues.zh: 做这些测量

cues.en: without messing up the wave.
cues.zh: 就不可能不扰动波。

cues.en: The interference pattern happens because the waves emerging from each slit are what we call coherent,
cues.zh: 干涉图案之所以出现，是因为从每条缝出来的波是我们所说的相干波，

cues.en: which is a fancy way of saying that the relationship between the waveforms emerging from the two slits,
cues.zh: 这不过是说，从两条缝出来的波形之间的关系，

cues.en: so locations
cues.zh: 也就是

cues.en: of peaks and valleys,
cues.zh: 波峰和波谷的位置，

cues.en: is predictable and stays consistent as the waves move forward.
cues.zh: 是可预测的，并且随着波向前传播保持一致。

cues.en: This coherence
cues.zh: 这种相干性

cues.en: is what allows the waves to produce the interference pattern in the first place.
cues.zh: 正是让波能够产生干涉图案的原因。

cues.en: But when you place some device in the path of either wave,
cues.zh: 但当你把某个装置放在其中任一束波的路径上，

cues.en: you mess with this coherence and so affect the pattern that reaches the screen.
cues.zh: 就会扰乱这种相干性，从而影响到达屏幕的图样。

cues.en: By the way, the double slit experiment where you try to determine which slit is traversed
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，在双缝实验中，如果你想确定粒子穿过的是哪条缝

cues.en: is called a which way experiment.
cues.zh: 这叫做哪条路径实验。

cues.en: And if the test is done on the far side of the slits,
cues.zh: 而如果测试是在狭缝的远端进行的，

cues.en: it's called a delayed choice experiment.
cues.zh: 就叫延迟选择实验。

cues.en: Physicists
cues.zh: 物理学家

cues.en: hate being outsmarted by the universe,
cues.zh: 讨厌被宇宙智商碾压，

cues.en: so they've come up with clever ways to measure which way the particle traveled while still preserving coherence.
cues.zh: 所以他们想出了巧妙的方法，在测量粒子走哪条路径的同时仍保持相干性。

cues.en: I'm gonna talk about the most famous
cues.zh: 我要讲的是最著名的

cues.en: performed in 1999.
cues.zh: 于1999年进行的实验。

cues.en: This experiment made use of a very special type of crystal that absorbs an incoming photon and creates two new photons,
cues.zh: 这个实验使用了一种非常特殊的晶体，它能吸收一个入射光子并产生两个新光子，

cues.en: each with half the energy of the original.
cues.zh: 每个新光子的能量都是原来光子的一半。

cues.en: These new photons are twins of each other. In fact, they're an entangled pair,
cues.zh: 这些新光子彼此成双。事实上，它们是一个纠缠对，

cues.en: so fundamentally connected in strange ways that we'll come back to. So place this crystal in front of the double slit to make coherent entangled pairs
cues.zh: 它们以奇怪的方式从根本上相连，这点我们后面再讲。所以把这块晶体放在双缝前，来产生相干的纠缠对

cues.en: of any photons passing through.
cues.zh: 由任何穿过的光子构成。

cues.en: Send one of each pair off to the screen to produce our interference pattern and use the other to figure out which slit the original photon passed through. Let's focus on detectors a and b here.
cues.zh: 把每对光子中的一个送到屏幕上形成干涉图案，用另一个来判断原始光子穿过了哪条缝。先关注这里的探测器 a 和 b。

cues.en: Detector a lights up if the original photon passed through slit a, and detector b lights up for slit b. If we run this for a bunch of photons, we see that whenever detectors a or b light up,
cues.zh: 如果原始光子穿过缝 a，探测器 a 就会亮起；如果穿过缝 b，探测器 b 就会亮起。我们对一批光子做这个实验，会发现只要探测器 a 或 b 亮起，

cues.en: we get a simple pile of photons here at the screen.
cues.zh: 我们在屏幕上只会得到简单的一堆光子。

cues.en: No interference pattern at all.
cues.zh: 完全没有干涉图样。

cues.en: It's as though any knowledge of which way the original photon traveled
cues.zh: 就好像只要知道了原始光子走了哪条路

cues.en: stops it from acting like a wave during its passage through the slits.
cues.zh: 它就没办法在穿过双缝时表现得像个波了。

cues.en: And crazier,
cues.zh: 更离谱的是，

cues.en: this experiment was set up so that photons reach a or b
cues.zh: 这个实验的设计是让光子先到达 a 或 b

cues.en: after their twins reach the screen.
cues.zh: 在它们的孪生光子到达屏幕之后。

cues.en: So a photon lands on the screen according to the pattern defined by its wave function. And then later, its entangled partner reaches detector a or b
cues.zh: 所以光子是按照它的波函数所确定的图样落在屏幕上。然后之后，它那纠缠的伙伴才到达探测器 a 或 b

cues.en: and somehow retroactively
cues.zh: 并且不知怎地，回溯性地

cues.en: influences the previous landing position.
cues.zh: 影响了它之前落下的位置。

cues.en: It's like the second photon is saying,
cues.zh: 就像第二个光子在说：

cues.en: woah. Woah. Woah. Someone figured out which slit I came through. You better look like you came through that one too.
cues.zh: 哇。哇。哇。有人弄清楚了我从哪条狭缝过来的。你最好也表现得像是从那条狭缝过来的一样。

cues.en: This is amazing.
cues.zh: 这太神奇了。

cues.en: And given that we only interact with one of the entangled pair, surely that means we aren't messing with the other, so we aren't ruining the interference pattern with decoherence.
cues.zh: 而且既然我们只与纠缠对中的一个发生相互作用，那肯定意味着我们没碰另一个，所以不会因退相干破坏干涉图样。

cues.en: Could it get any weirder?
cues.zh: 还能更离奇吗？

cues.en: This is quantum mechanics. So, yeah,
cues.zh: 这就是量子力学。所以，没错，

cues.en: this extra stuff is the quantum eraser.
cues.zh: 这些额外的东西就是量子擦除器。

cues.en: Its job is to destroy any information
cues.zh: 它的任务是摧毁任何信息

cues.en: about the path of the photons.
cues.zh: 关于光子路径的信息。

cues.en: These devices are beam splitters,
cues.zh: 这些装置是分束器，

cues.en: just half silvered mirrors.
cues.zh: 也就是半透半反镜。

cues.en: They work by allowing 50% of the photons through while reflecting the other 50 percents.
cues.zh: 它们让50%的光子通过，反射另外50%。

cues.en: Now you have a new possible outcome.
cues.zh: 现在你有了一个新的可能结果。

cues.en: Instead of being reflected to detectors a or b, half of the photons end up in detectors c or d.
cues.zh: 一半光子不再被反射到探测器a或b，而是进入探测器c或d。

cues.en: But this clever arrangement
cues.zh: 但这种巧妙的安排

cues.en: ensures that if c or d light up, we have no idea which slit that photon came from.
cues.zh: 确保了如果c或d亮起，我们就不知道那个光子来自哪条狭缝。

cues.en: If we only look at the photons whose twins end up at detector c or d,
cues.zh: 如果我们只看那些孪生光子最终到达探测器 c 或 d 的情况，

cues.en: we do see an interference pattern.
cues.zh: 我们确实会看到干涉图样。

cues.en: It looks like the simple act of scrambling the which way information
cues.zh: 看起来，仅仅是打乱路径信息这个动作，

cues.en: retroactively sends the message,
cues.zh: 就回溯性地传回了消息：

cues.en: okay, chill. The observer lost the info of which slit we went through. It's safe to have gone through both again.
cues.zh: 好吧，冷静点。观察者丢失了我们经过哪条缝的信息。那就可以安全地再次同时穿过两条缝了。

cues.en: Are we forced to double down on the interpretation that observation of the path causes the collapse of the wave function,
cues.zh: 难道我们非得一口咬定这种解释：对路径的观察导致波函数坍缩，

cues.en: and that the wave function can collapse
cues.zh: 而且波函数可以坍缩

cues.en: all the way back to wherever our new knowledge extends to in the past,
cues.zh: 一直回溯到我们新获得的知识在过去所延伸到的任何地方，

cues.en: some sort of retroactive reality cascade?
cues.zh: 某种回溯性的现实级联？

cues.en: This is a pretty wild story.
cues.zh: 这故事挺离谱的。

cues.en: For that reason, it makes sense to be cautious,
cues.zh: 因此，保持谨慎是合理的，

cues.en: even of the Copenhagen interpretation.
cues.zh: 哪怕是对哥本哈根诠释。

cues.en: Part of the appeal of the Copenhagen interpretation is that it avoids any physical interaction
cues.zh: 哥本哈根诠释的吸引力之一，在于它避免了任何物理相互作用

cues.en: that moves faster than light.
cues.zh: 也就是超光速的相互作用。

cues.en: See, when spread out wave function resolves itself into a set of known properties,
cues.zh: 你看，当弥散的波函数归结为一组已知属性时，

cues.en: say the location of a particle on the double slit screen,
cues.zh: 比如粒子在双缝屏幕上的位置，

cues.en: somehow the entire wave function knows to do this,
cues.zh: 不知怎么的，整个波函数知道要这样做，

cues.en: to collapse at the same instant.
cues.zh: 在同一瞬间坍缩。

cues.en: But if these wave functions aren't physical,
cues.zh: 但如果这些波函数不是物理的，

cues.en: as the Copenhagen interpretation would tell us,
cues.zh: 正如哥本哈根诠释告诉我们的那样，

cues.en: then there's no real instantaneous
cues.zh: 那就不存在真正瞬时的

cues.en: physical interaction.
cues.zh: 物理相互作用。

cues.en: By contrast,
cues.zh: 相比之下，

cues.en: a physical interpretation of the wave function,
cues.zh: 对波函数作物理诠释，

cues.en: like the de Broglie Bohm pilot wave theory, requires an underlying physicality,
cues.zh: 比如德布罗意-玻姆导波理论，就需要一种底层的物理性，

cues.en: a set of defined properties
cues.zh: 一组确定的属性

cues.en: that evolves with the wave function,
cues.zh: 它们随波函数演化，

cues.en: so called hidden variables.
cues.zh: 也就是所谓的隐变量。

cues.en: That's a bit uncomfortable because to explain experimental results,
cues.zh: 这有点让人不安，因为要解释实验结果，

cues.en: those physical properties
cues.zh: 那些物理属性

cues.en: need to act and change instantly at any distance.
cues.zh: 必须在任意距离上瞬时作用和变化。

cues.en: They need to have what we call non locality.
cues.zh: 它们需要具备我们所说的非定域性。

cues.en: Now the delayed choice quantum eraser double slit experiment
cues.zh: 现在来看延迟选择量子擦除双缝实验

cues.en: doesn't tell us whether the wave function is physical or not,
cues.zh: 它并不能告诉我们波函数是否是物理实在，

cues.en: but it tells us that the Copenhagen
cues.zh: 但它告诉我们，哥本哈根

cues.en: or any other metaphysical interpretation of the wave function
cues.zh: 或任何其他对波函数的形而上学诠释

cues.en: is no less, well, crazy sounding than a physical interpretation.
cues.zh: 嗯，听起来并不比物理解释更不疯狂。

cues.en: In fact, the solution may lie in this fascinating phenomenon of quantum entanglement.
cues.zh: 事实上，答案可能就在于量子纠缠这一迷人现象之中。

cues.en: As we'll see in the future, entangled particles
cues.zh: 我们之后会看到，纠缠粒子

cues.en: really are able to influence each other instantaneously,
cues.zh: 确实能瞬间相互影响，

cues.en: and we'll see that their non locality
cues.zh: 我们还会看到，它们的非定域性

cues.en: doesn't violate causality.
cues.zh: 并不违反因果性。

cues.en: So perhaps they can even affect coherence and decoherence
cues.zh: 所以也许它们甚至能影响相干性和退相干

cues.en: retroactively
cues.zh: 回溯性地

cues.en: and physically
cues.zh: 并且在物理层面

cues.en: without making a causal mess.
cues.zh: 又不会造成因果混乱。

cues.en: Perhaps this thing we call observation
cues.zh: 也许我们所谓的“观测”

cues.en: is just entanglement between the observer and the experiment.
cues.zh: 不过是观测者与实验之间的纠缠。

cues.en: Perhaps the evolving tapestry of entanglement
cues.zh: 也许那不断演化的纠缠图景

cues.en: in all its impossible complexity
cues.zh: 以其难以想象的复杂性

cues.zh: 访问 audible.com/spacetime

cues.zh: 获取他们的音频节目和有声作品。

cues.en: I recently listened to The Big Picture by Sean Carroll.
cues.zh: 我最近听了 Sean Carroll 的《The Big Picture》。

cues.en: It's rare to find a brilliant theoretical physicist
cues.zh: 很难得遇到一位杰出的理论物理学家

cues.en: who's willing and able to discuss the philosophical and human implications of the science
cues.zh: 愿意并且能够讨论科学在哲学和人类层面的意义

cues.en: without the nonsense mysticism.
cues.zh: 而不掺那些胡扯的神秘主义。

cues.zh: 前往 audible.com/spacetime，

cues.en: and make sure you use that link so they know we sent you and to get a membership trial.
cues.zh: 并务必使用那个链接，让他们知道是我们推荐的，还能获得会员试用。

cues.en: Last week, Neil Stevenson came on the show to help us figure out how to save humanity from the end of the world.
cues.zh: 上周，Neil Stevenson 来到节目，帮我们想办法如何从世界末日中拯救人类。

cues.en: You guys had your own ideas.
cues.zh: 你们大家也有自己的想法。

cues.en: Mosai Kitsune asks, what if a black hole was headed towards the Earth? Could we stop it? This is a great end of world scenario, and the short answer is no.
cues.zh: Mosai Kitsune 问：如果一个黑洞正朝地球飞来会怎样？我们能阻止它吗？这是个很棒的世界末日场景，简短回答是：不能。

cues.en: Long answer, depends on the type of black hole and how close it gets. The only black holes that we know for sure are buzzing around our galaxy are stellar remnant black holes and are at least several times the mass of the sun.
cues.zh: 长答案取决于黑洞的类型以及它离得多近。我们唯一确定正在银河系中四处游荡的黑洞是恒星残骸黑洞，而且质量至少是太阳的数倍。

cues.en: Something like that passing through the solar system,
cues.zh: 这样的天体穿过太阳系，

cues.en: even if nowhere near the Earth, would probably disrupt planetary orbits and either rearrange or scatter our planetary system.
cues.zh: 即使离地球很远，也很可能会扰乱行星轨道，要么重新排列、要么打散我们的行星系统。

cues.en: Even if it passed by the outer reaches of the solar system, it would perturb the Oort cloud and send swarms of comets plummeting inwards.
cues.zh: 即使它只是掠过太阳系外缘，也会扰动奥尔特云，让成群的彗星向内侧坠落。

cues.en: However, there's a theoretical type of black hole, so called primordial black holes,
cues.zh: 不过，理论上还存在一种黑洞，即所谓的原初黑洞，

cues.en: which may have formed in the first instance after the Big Bang.
cues.zh: 它们可能是在大爆炸之后的最初阶段形成的。

cues.en: These may have masses similar to planets rather than stars, if they exist.
cues.zh: 如果它们存在，质量可能与行星相近，而非恒星。

cues.en: And one of these passing through the solar system would only be dangerous if it was moving slowly enough and if it came very close to the Earth.
cues.zh: 而其中一个穿过太阳系时，只有速度足够慢、并且离地球非常近，才会造成危险。

cues.en: In fact, impact by a primordial black hole was one of the hypotheses that Seveneve's scientists proposed for the moon's inexplicable destruction.
cues.zh: 事实上，原初黑洞撞击是 Seveneve 的科学家为月球莫名毁灭提出的假说之一。

cues.en: TSJoinCinema
cues.zh: TSJoinCinema

cues.en: would to know what would exactly happen if a gamma ray burst hit the Earth.
cues.zh: 想知道如果伽马射线暴击中地球，究竟会发生什么。

cues.en: I'm glad you asked. By happy coincidence, the wonderful channel Kurzgesagt
cues.zh: 很高兴你问了。很巧，超棒的频道 Kurzgesagt

cues.en: recently published a whole episode on gamma ray bursts.
cues.zh: 最近刚发布了一整集讲伽马射线暴的内容。

cues.en: I'll let them answer this one for you. Check the link. A few of you pointed out that I neglected to mention certain known ends of the world that are coming in the distant future. And, yeah, sure, Earth is certainly doomed. The increasing temperature of the sun will cause all of Earth's oceans to evaporate
cues.zh: 这个问题我让他们来替你回答。看链接。你们中有几个人指出，我漏提了一些已知的、会在遥远未来发生的世界末日。嗯，当然，地球肯定在劫难逃。太阳温度不断升高，会导致地球上所有海洋蒸发

cues.en: in a billion years, plus or minus, depending on the model.
cues.zh: 大约十亿年后，具体误差取决于模型。

cues.en: But that's the sort of predictable event that hopefully a super advanced post humanity can deal with with a bit of basic geoengineering,
cues.zh: 但这类可预测的事件，希望超级先进的“后人类”能用一点基础的地球工程手段来应对，

cues.en: increasing atmospheric reflectivity,
cues.zh: 提高大气反射率，

cues.en: for example, which is something we could do in the very near future if we wanted to.
cues.zh: 比如，只要我们愿意，在不久的将来就能做到。

cues.en: As for the death of the sun and Andromeda's collision with the Milky Way,
cues.zh: 至于太阳的死亡，以及仙女座星系与银河系的碰撞，

cues.en: okay. Let's deal with one end of the world at a time, people. I also asked you to submit your ideas for extinction proofing humanity.
cues.zh: 好吧。各位，我们一次处理一个世界末日。我还让大家提交过如何让人类免于灭绝的想法。

cues.en: The prize,
cues.zh: 奖品是，

cues.en: a place on the ark.
cues.zh: 方舟上的一个位置。

cues.en: Here are the winners. In the event of end of world, you guys should show up at your local spaceport.
cues.zh: 以下是获奖者。万一世界末日来临，你们就到当地航天港报到。

cues.en: Your names will be on the door list. Era four zero four, heard or not found, had a great idea in which you collect asteroids
cues.zh: 你们的名字会列在门口的名单上。Era four zero four 提出过一个很棒的构想：收集小行星，

cues.en: and put them in orbit around the Earth,
cues.zh: 把它们放到绕地球的轨道上，

cues.en: ready to sling at any oncoming impactors before they reach us. This is actually a really nice one. The rocks don't even have to be all that big. As long as you spot the incoming rock on one of its near Earth passes before the impact pass,
cues.zh: 随时准备在来袭的撞击体到达我们之前把它甩出去。这其实是个非常好的点子。那些石头甚至不用很大。只要你在来袭岩石某次接近地球的飞掠过程中发现它，而那还不是撞击的那一次，

cues.en: you could play little cosmic billiards to knock it just off course.
cues.zh: 你就可以玩一场小小的宇宙台球，把它撞得偏离轨道。

cues.en: Timak TR suggests we upload our minds into deep underground computers.
cues.zh: Timak TR 建议我们把意识上传到地下深处的计算机里。

cues.en: Go full virtual? I'm down with that. Although, who's to say we didn't already do that? Caleb Tandberg wants to build underwater cities instead of underground cities to protect against gamma ray bursts.
cues.zh: 完全虚拟化？我赞成。不过，谁又能说我们不是已经这么做了呢？Caleb Tandberg 想建水下城市而不是地下城市，来抵御伽马射线暴。

cues.en: I really love this idea. You don't even need much water at all to fully protect us from the gamma ray burst or subsequent UV.
cues.zh: 我真的很喜欢这个想法。甚至不需要多少水，就能完全保护我们免受伽马射线暴或随后紫外线的影响。

cues.en: So just below the surface is great.
cues.zh: 所以就在水面之下就很好。

cues.en: All surface life is laid waste,
cues.zh: 所有地表生命都被毁灭了，

cues.en: but, hey, the deathless face of the unborn mind has an extinction proofing idea.
cues.zh: 但是，嘿，未生之心的不死面孔有一个防灭绝的点子。

cues.en: Reinvent our monetary economic systems to produce efficient, stable, and healthier societies
cues.zh: 重新发明我们的货币经济体系，以产生高效、稳定、更健康的社会

cues.en: that actually have the energy and collective intelligence to progress technologically.
cues.zh: 这些社会真正拥有推动技术进步的能源和集体智慧。

cues.en: Okay. Well, if you're gonna be sensible about it,
cues.zh: 好吧。如果你要这么务实的话，

cues.en: but could we please still have the underwater cities?
cues.zh: 但我们还能不能保留水下城市？
